name: Nebat
title: Jeroboam's father
summary: Nebat is best known as the father of Jeroboam, the first king of Israel after the kingdom was divided. He is mentioned repeatedly in the Bible as an identifier for his son, who is referred to as "Jeroboam, son of Nebat." Nebat himself played no direct role in the biblical accounts, but his name is inseparably linked to Jeroboam's sin and rebellion against Rehoboam.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Jeroboam's father
keyEvents.description: Nebat is identified as the father of Jeroboam, the servant of Solomon who rose up against the king.

keyEvents.title: Jeroboam's rebellion against Solomon
keyEvents.description: Jeroboam, son of Nebat, lifted his hand against King Solomon. Nebat is mentioned here as an identifier for his son.

keyEvents.title: Jeroboam becomes king over Israel
keyEvents.description: After Solomon's death and the division of the kingdom, Jeroboam, son of Nebat, became king over the ten northern tribes of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Jeroboam's sin attributed to the son of Nebat
keyEvents.description: The expression "Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin" becomes a recurring formula throughout the Books of Kings as a reference to idol worship.

keyEvents.title: Nebat's origin from Ephraim
keyEvents.description: Nebat is described as an Ephrathite from Zeredah, placing him in the tribe of Ephraim and providing background for Jeroboam's position.

keyEvents.title: Jeroboam's calf worship linked to Nebat's name
keyEvents.description: Nebat's name is repeatedly connected to the sin his son introduced by setting up golden calves in Bethel and Dan.
